title: Publish public-friendly Enterprise Security overview in redwood-docs (link to gated evidence request process)
creator: Naomi Feldman
content:
## Context
Enterprise prospects are increasingly blocked on security/compliance review. Sales and SEs need a canonical, public-friendly page they can link early in the process (before NDAs), while keeping sensitive evidence (SOC 2 report, pentest summaries, subprocessor details beyond the public list, etc.) behind the evidence request workflow.

This ticket adds/refreshes a public "Enterprise Security" overview in redwood-docs with:
- High-level, accurate security posture language aligned with the refreshed Confluence Security FAQ
- Deployment-mode framing (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private)
- Clear guidance on what we *can* share publicly vs what requires an NDA
- Links to the gated SOC 2 / evidence request process (not direct artifact links)

## Goals
1) Provide a single, stable link Sales/SE can send for baseline security posture.
2) Reduce time spent answering repeat questions by pointing to canonical docs.
3) Avoid over-claiming: do not promise roadmap items; do not imply ISO certification if not certified.

## Non-goals
- Publishing restricted artifacts (SOC 2 report, detailed pentest report, internal policies)
- Introducing new product capabilities or committing to roadmap

## Proposed doc structure (redwood-docs)
Page: /enterprise/security (final URL may vary based on docs IA)

Sections:
1. Overview (what Redwood covers / shared responsibility high-level)
2. Data handling & privacy (no training on customer data; retention/deletion basics; see retention/residency page)
3. Encryption & key management (in-transit/at-rest; deployment differences; where KMS details live)
4. Identity & access (SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC; links to product docs where available)
5. Audit logging (what events we log; export options; retention knobs)
6. Vulnerability management & incident response (high-level statements; no specifics that are evidence-only)
7. Compliance & reports (SOC 2: how to request under NDA; ISO alignment wording guidance)
8. Subprocessors (link to canonical subprocessor list page if exists; otherwise refer to "available upon request")
9. Evidence request (CTA: link to playbook/form; define expected turnaround time)

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] New/updated public docs page is merged to redwood-docs main and deployed.
- [x] Page includes explicit wording: SOC 2 report available under NDA via evidence request process.
- [x] No direct links to restricted Google Drive/Confluence folders.
- [x] Language matches approved guidance in enablement kit (no ISO certification claim; no absolute data residency guarantees without caveats).
- [x] Includes deployment-mode qualifiers where behavior differs (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- [x] Includes stable outbound links that Sales can reuse (avoid branch links).
- [x] Reviewed by Security/GRC and Product Security PM before merge.

## Implementation notes
- Add page under docs nav "Security" or "Enterprise" (Docs team to confirm IA).
- Keep statements capability-based and verifiable. Avoid numbers/frequencies unless already approved (e.g., pen-test cadence) and stable.
- Where detailed behavior is changing (retention wording), link to the customer-facing retention overview that is maintained by Security/GRC.
- Add a short "Last updated" and "Questions?" block with correct aliases.

## Review checklist (must-do)
- Security technical review: Marcus Lin
- GRC review: Olga Petrov or Daniel Carter
- PM alignment: Naomi Feldman
- Messaging consistency: Camila Reyes / Soojin Lee (lightweight)

## Rollout plan
- After docs deploy: update Confluence enablement kit index to point to the public page.
- Provide Sales snippet text for outbound emails: "For an overview of Redwood’s security posture, see: <link>. For the SOC 2 report and additional evidence, request via: <evidence link>".

## Notes on wording constraints (do/don’t)
DO:
- "SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA upon request"
- "Supports SSO (SAML 2.0)" / "SCIM provisioning supported" (where true)
- "Encryption in transit and at rest"
- "Private deployment options for regulated workloads"

DON’T:
- "ISO 27001 certified" (unless/ until certified)
- "We never retain any data" (retention is deployment- and configuration-dependent)
- "We do not use any subprocessors" (not accurate)
- Any promise of future feature delivery

## Links
- GitHub PR: sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2841-add-enterprise-security-overview-page.json
- Related docs PRs:
  - sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2849-document-audit-logging-and-export-options.json
  - sources/github/redwood-docs/pr-2860-clarify-data-retention-and-residency-language.json
- Evidence request process (internal canonical): sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/soc2-customer-evidence-request-playbook.json
- Internal reference for SSO/RBAC: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth/sso-saml-scim-and-rbac-capabilities.json

## Open questions
- Do we have a public subprocessor list URL already? If not, we should add a stub page that explains how to request the current list.
- Confirm whether we should call the page "Enterprise Security" vs "Security & Trust" (Marketing preference).

2026-01-29 (Marcus Lin): Reviewed draft. Requested edits: add deployment-mode qualifiers to retention statement; clarify that audit log export destinations depend on customer configuration.

2026-02-06 (Olga Petrov): GRC pass. Approved SOC 2 phrasing: "SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA" and "additional evidence on request". Removed mention of "ISO-ready".

2026-02-12 (Camila Reyes): Messaging tweaks: emphasize shared responsibility model and avoid security-superlatives.

2026-02-18 (Elliot Price): Merged PR-2841 and confirmed docs deploy in next publish window. Sent final link to Stephanie Nguyen for Sales training deck update.

2026-02-21 (Talia Benson): Marking Done. Please add to enablement-kit link tracker and ensure HubSpot snippet references the canonical URL (not GitHub).
